title: Beyond Sample-Level Forgetting: Improving Reliability in Multimodal Unlearning
claim: Existing unlearning methods that forget a target also damage related knowledge, which makes them ineffective, unreliable and non-local in use.
layout: 2 stacked panels: (a) left-to-right flow with bar charts, (b) three chat boxes
description: The figure has two parts. Panel (a), 'Unlearning of VLMs', shows photos of Steve Jobs (forget image), a forget-text box, and Tim Cook (remaining image). Arrows feed them into a dotted box with 3D blocks for visual and textual knowledge. Blue arrows link the blocks, and a red X marks the severed links. To the right, two boxes compare original and unlearned prediction bar charts for CEO, male and beard. Green checks and red crosses mark which attributes were correctly forgotten or wrongly affected. Panel (b), 'Downstream Application', has three chat scenarios. A user asks about Jobs and gets a forgotten answer (effective). An attacker gets an outlier description (not reliable). A user asks about Tim Cook and gets a wrong answer (not local). The eye goes first to the photos and the red and green marks.
caption: After forgetting, current multimodal unlearning methods
abstract: Multimodal unlearning aims to eliminate specific data from pretrained multimodal models, which offers significant advantages in data privacy and model efficiency. Current methods struggle to achieve the desired properties of effectiveness, reliability and locality, due to the complex interdependency of unimodal and multimodal knowledge. By introducing a causal perspective, we propose multimodal unlearning with decoupled knowledge components. To promote fine-grained understanding of multimodal context, we introduce Multimodal Variational Inference (MVI) to infer modal-specific and -consistent factors with incomplete sample observation. With foundation of decoupled knowledge, we propose contrastive semantic editing to regulate multimodal unlearning towards refined forgetting. Experiments on privacy- and copyright-sensitive scenarios validate effectiveness of our method across multiple scenarios, ensuring the unlearned model maintains high reliability and locality.
